images.title: West coast and east coast cities
images.purpose: Places the six rainfall cities on a plain outline of India in two coastal groups.
images.composition: A large plain outline of India centred in the frame, three teal pins on the west coast and three amber pins on the east coast, with a coast label on each side. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A plain outline of India with no state borders, light fill, thin dark outline. Three teal (#0072B2) pins on the west coast labelled, from south to north, 'Kovalam', 'Udupi' and 'Mumbai'. Three amber (#E69F00) pins on the east coast labelled, from south to north, 'Rameswaram', 'Chennai' and 'Puri'. In the sea to the west, the teal label 'west coast'; in the sea to the east, the amber label 'east coast'. Exactly 6 pins.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The six cities sit in two groups, three on the west coast and three on the east coast.
images.description: Places the six rainfall cities on a plain outline of India in two coastal groups.
images.context: West coast cities peak June to August; Rameswaram and Chennai October to December; Puri July to September.
images.teaching_notes: Peak months stay in the video and graphs; the map carries only the grouping.

image_decisions.why: Grouping the cities by coast is the first step to reading their rain peaks; a map shows it at a glance.
